title: Proof
body_md:
Since the image of $d$ is
orthogonal to the image of $\delta$ in
$L^2(E)$, we get
$\| D\phi\|_0^2=
\| d\phi\|_0^2+\|\delta\phi\|_0^2$ for any $\phi\inC^\infty(E)$. Thus
$$\| d\phi\|_0+\|\delta\phi\|_0\leq\sqrt{2}\,\| D\phi\|_0\;.\quad\Box
head: manual
name: property $($vi$)$ for $k=0$

title: Proof
body_md:
This property follows from (\ref{e:norm}) since, for $\phi\in W^{l+1}(E)$,
we have
the following:
$$\left\| e^{-t{\Delta}}\phi\right\|_l\leq c_{l,1}\,\|\phi\|_l\leq
c_{l,1}e_{l,2}\,\|\phi\|_{l+1}\;,$$
$$\left\| D\,e^{-t{\Delta}}\phi\right\|_l=
\left\|e^{-t{\Delta}}\,D\phi\right\|_l\leq c_{l,1}\,\|D\phi\|_l\leq
c_{l,1}e_{l,2}\,\|\phi\|_{l+1}\;,$$
\begin{eqnarray*}
\left\|A\,e^{-t{\Delta}}\phi\right\|_l&\leq&\left\|\left[A,e^{-t{\Delta}}\right]\phi
\right\|_l+
\left\|e^{-t{\Delta}}\,A\phi\right\|_l\\
&\leq&\tilde c_{l,1}\,\|\phi\|_l+  c_{l,1}\,\|A\phi\|_l\\
&\leq&(\tilde c_{l,1}+c_{l,1})e_{l,2}\,\|\phi\|_{l+1}\;,
\end{eqnarray*}
where we have used property~(i) for $k=l$, Lemma~\ref{l:[A,e]} and
(\ref{e:norm}).~$\Box$
head: manual
name: property $($i$)$ for $k=l+1$

title: Proof
body_md:
Again this property follows from (\ref{e:norm}) since, for $\phi\in
W^{l+1}(E)$ we
have the following:
$$\left\| D\,e^{-t{\Delta}}\phi \right\|_l\leq
\frac{c_{l,2}}{\sqrt{t}}\|\phi\|_l
\leq\frac{c_{l,2}e_{l,2}}{\sqrt{t}}\,\|\phi\|_{l+1}\;,$$
$$\left\|{\Delta} \,e^{-t{\Delta}}\phi\right\|_l=\left\|D\,e^{-t{\Delta}}\,D\phi\right\|_l\leq
\frac{c_{l,2}}{\sqrt{t}}\,\|D\phi\|_l\leq
\frac{c_{l,2}e_{l,2}}{\sqrt{t}}\,\|\phi\|_{l+1}\;,$$
\begin{eqnarray*}
\left\|AD\,e^{-t{\Delta}}\phi\right\|_l&\leq&\left\|\left(AD\,e^{-t{\Delta}}\pm
D\,e^{-t{\Delta}}\,A\right)\phi\right\|_l+\left\|D\,e^{-t{\Delta}}
\,A\phi\right\|_l\\
&\leq&\frac{\tilde c_{l,2}}{\sqrt{t}}\,\|\phi\|_l+
\frac{c_{l,2}}{\sqrt{t}}\,\|A\phi\|_l\\
&\leq&\frac{(\tilde c_{l,2}+c_{l,2})e_{l,2}}{\sqrt{t}}\,\|\phi\|_{l+1}\;,
\end{eqnarray*}
where we have used property~(ii) for $k=l$, Lemma~\ref{l:ADe+-De} and
(\ref{e:norm}).~$\Box$
head: manual
name: property $($ii$)$ for $k=l+1$

title: Proof
body_md:
This follows directly from property~(ii) for $k=l+1$ since
${\Delta} \,e^{-t{\Delta}}=D\,e^{-t{\Delta}/2}\,D\,e^{-t{\Delta}/2}$ on $C^\infty(E)$.~$\Box$
head: manual
name: property $($iii$)$ for $k=l+1$

label: e:composition1
title: Proof
head: manual
name: property $($iv$)$ for $k=l+1$

title: Proof
body_md:
By Corollary~\ref{c:bounded Pi} and property~(v) for $k=l$, $\Pi$ defines a
projection of $W^{l+1}(E)$ onto the kernel of ${\Delta}$ in $W^{l+1}(E)$.

Now, for $t>0$ and
$s\in{\bf R}$ let
$$
f_t(s)=\left\{
\begin{array}{cl}
(1-e^{-ts^2})/s^2& \mbox{if}\quad s\neq 0\\
t& \mbox{if}\quad s=0\;.
\end{array}
\right.
$$
It is easy to  check that $f_t$ is in the algebra $\cal A$ of
Proposition~\ref{p:finite time}. Thus $f_t(D)$ defines a bounded operator on
$W^{l+1}(E)$ satisfying
$$\mbox{\rm id}-e^{-t{\Delta}}={\Delta}\,f_t(D)\;.$$
So property~(iv) for $k=l+1$ yields that,  for any $\phi\in
W^{l+1}(E)$, $\widetilde\Pi\phi$ is the limit of
${\Delta} f_t(D)\phi$ in $W^{l+1}(E)$ as $t\rightarrow\infty$. Hence
$$\widetilde\Pi(W^{l+1}(E))\subset\mbox{\rm cl}_{l+1}(\mbox{\rm im}\;{\Delta})\;.$$
This is really an equality because the reverse inclusion can be easily proved as
follows:
\begin{eqnarray*}
\mbox{\rm cl}_{l+1}(\mbox{\rm im}\;{\Delta})&\subset&W^{l+1}(E)\cap\mbox{\rm cl}_0(\mbox{\rm im}\;{\Delta})\\
&=&W^{l+1}(E)\cap\widetilde\Pi\left(L^2(E)\right)\\
&=&\widetilde\Pi\left(W^{l+1}(E)\right)\;.
\end{eqnarray*}
Here we have used property~(v) for $k=0$ and the fact
that $\widetilde\Pi$ is a projection. Therefore we have proved the
first direct sum decomposition in property~(v) for $k=l+1$.

The second direct sum decomposition follows similarly by using the
functions given by
$$
g_t(s)=\left\{
\begin{array}{cl}
(1-e^{-ts^2})/s& \mbox{if}\quad s\neq 0\\
t& \mbox{if}\quad s=0
\end{array}
\right.
$$
instead of the $f_t$.~$\Box$
head: manual
name: property $($v$)$ for $k=l+1$

title: Proof
body_md:
Take any $\phi\inC^\infty(E)$.
Lemma~\ref{l:key'}, property~(vi) for $k=l$ and
(\ref{e:norm''}) yield
\begin{eqnarray*}
\|d\phi\|_{l+1}+\|\delta\phi\|_{l+1}&\leq&
\frac{1}{e_{l,1}''}\left(\|d\phi\|_l+\|\delta\phi\|_l+
\|Dd\phi\|_l+\|D\delta\phi\|_l\right.\\
& &\left.\mbox{}+\|(A-B_1)d\phi\|_l+\|(A-B_1)\delta\phi\|_l\right)\\
&\leq&\frac{1}{e_{l,1}''}\left(\|d\phi\|_l+\|\delta\phi\|_l+
\|dD\phi\|_l+\|\delta D\phi\|_l\right.\\
& &\left.\mbox{}+\|d(\mp A+B_2)\phi\|_l+\|\delta(\mp A+B_2)\phi\|_l\right)\\
&\leq&\frac{c_{l,4}}{e_{l,1}''}\left(\|D\phi\|_l+
\|{\Delta}\phi\|_l+\|D(\mp A+B_2)\phi\|_l\right)\\
&\leq&\frac{c_{l,4}}{e_{l,1}''}\left(\|D\phi\|_l+
\|{\Delta}\phi\|_l+\|(A-B_1)D\phi\|_l\right)\\
&\leq&\frac{c_{l,4}e_{l,2}''}{e_{l,1}''}
\,\|D\phi\|_{l+1}\;.\quad\Box
head: manual
name: property $($vi$)$ for $k=l+1$

label: rem:symmetric A
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:symmetric A}
If $A$ is symmetric in Theorem~\ref{t:general}, then one of the two equations in
$($\ref{e:key}$)$ can be removed in its statement because both of them
are equivalent  by taking adjoints on $M$.
head: environment

label: rem:more general
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:more general}
The following more general condition can be
used instead of $($\ref{e:key}$)$ in Theorem~\ref{t:general} to get the
same long time
behavior of leafwise heat flow with a similar proof: There is some first order
transversely elliptic differential operator $A$ and zero order operators
$K_1,\ldots,K_{16}$ such that the operators
\begin{eqnarray*} F_1&=&Ad\pm dA-K_1d-dK_2-K_3\delta-\delta K_4 \;,\\
F_2&=&A\delta\pm\delta A-K_5\delta-\delta K_6-K_7d-dK_8
\end{eqnarray*}
satisfy
\begin{eqnarray*}
\lefteqn{F_1\delta\mp\delta F_1+F_2d\mp dF_2=}\\
&&dK_9d+\delta K_{10}d+dK_{11}\delta+\delta
K_{12}\delta+d\delta K_{13}+\delta dK_{14}+K_{15}d\delta+K_{16}\delta d\;.
\end{eqnarray*}
Nevertheless, so far we did not find any non-Riemannian
foliation with a $($non-elliptic$)$ leafwise elliptic differential complex
satisfying such a more general
condition.
head: environment

label: rem:K=L
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:K=L}
Proposition~\ref{p:de Rham} is slightly stronger than~$($\ref{e:key}$)$
in Theorem~\ref{t:general}. In this case $K=L$, and thus 
$$D_\perp D_0+D_0 D_\perp= B_1D_0+D_0B_2$$
with
$$B_1=K^\ast P+KQ\;,\quad B_2=QK^\ast+PK$$
in Lemma~\ref{l:key'}. In particular $B_2=B_1^\ast$. 
Observe that, if $K$ is symmetric,
then so is $B_1$, yielding that $D_\perp-B_1$ commutes with 
${\Delta}_0$ and thus with
$e^{-t{\Delta}_0}$. Therefore the proof of Theorem~\ref{t:de Rham} 
would follow with a much
simpler induction argument. Of course $K$ is not symmetric in general.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
The above proof of Proposition~\ref{p:de Rham} gives explicit
local descriptions of $K$ and $L$. But an alternative 
proof can be made by using
Molino's description of Riemannian foliations: 
It allows to reduce the proof to the
case of transversely parallelizable foliations, 
where our local arguments can be made
globally.
head: environment

label: rem:[Dperp,Pi]
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:[Dperp,Pi]}
In the setting of this section, Corollary~\ref{c:[A,Pi]} states that 
$[D_\perp,\Pi]$
defines a bounded operator on each $W^k\Omega$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
Let $E(\lambda)$ and $\widetilde E\left(\tilde\lambda\right)$ 
be the eigenspaces
corresponding to eigenvalues $\lambda$ of ${\Delta}_1$ and 
$\tilde\lambda$ of
$\widetilde{\Delta}_1$. This eigenspaces have bigradings 
induced by the bigradings of ${\cal
H}_1$ and 
$\widetilde{\cal H}_1$. Then, if $M$ is oriented, 
the Hodge star operator also
induces duality $E(\lambda)^{u,v}\cong E(\lambda)^{q-u,p-v}$, and skew
duality $\widetilde E\left(\tilde\lambda\right)^{u,v}\cong\widetilde
E\left(\tilde\lambda\right)^{q-u-1,p-v+1}$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
If we use appropriate zero order modifications of $D_\perp$, then 
we get the Hodge
theoretic version of the results of \cite{Demetrio}, which 
have important implications
about tenseness.

label: mc:de Rham
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{mc:de Rham}
With the above notation, assume that $\widehat\mathcal{F}$ is a Riemannian foliation. Then $\Pi$
defines a continuous operator on $\Omega(\mathcal{F},V)$, we have the leafwise Hodge
decomposition
$$\Omega(\mathcal{F},V)=\ker\Delta_\mathcal{F}\oplus\overline{\operatorname{im}\Delta_\mathcal{F}} =(\ker
d_\mathcal{F}\cap\ker\delta_\mathcal{F})\oplus\overline{\operatorname{im} d_\mathcal{F}}\oplus
\overline{\operatorname{im}\delta_\mathcal{F}}\;,$$
and $(t,\alpha)\mapsto e^{-t\Delta_\mathcal{F}}\alpha$ defines a continuous map
$[0,\infty]\times\Omega(\mathcal{F},V)\to\Omega(\mathcal{F},V)$.
Thus ${\mathcal H}(\mathcal{F},V)$ can be canonically identified with $\ker\Delta_\mathcal{F}$, and,
if $\mathcal{F}$ is oriented, then the leafwise Hodge star operator on $\ker\Delta_\mathcal{F}$ induces an
isomorphism ${\mathcal H}^v(\mathcal{F},V)\cong{\mathcal H}^{p-v}(\mathcal{F},V^\ast)$.
head: environment

label: ex: Goette
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex: Goette}
Consider $\mathbb{S}^1\equiv\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z}$, and let $[x]\in \mathbb{S}^1$ denote the class of every $x\in\mathbb{R}$. Take the 2-torus $M = \mathbb{S}^1\times \mathbb{S}^1$ with the foliation $\mathcal{F}$ whose leaves are the fibers of the first factor projection to $\mathbb{S}^1$. It is the quotient of the foliation $\widetilde\mathcal{F}$ on $\widetilde M :=\mathbb{R}^2$ whose leaves are the fibers of the first factor projection to $\mathbb{R}$. Let $V$ be the complex line bundle over $M$ that is the quotient of the trivial complex line bundle $\widetilde V := \widetilde M\times\mathbb{C}$ over $\widetilde M$ by the action of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ defined by the transformations 
\[
T_{m,n}(x,y,z) = (x+2\pi m, y+2\pi n, e^{2\pi n \sin(x) i} z),
\]
where $i = \sqrt{-1}$ and $m,n \in\mathbb{Z}$. Consider also the trivial Hermitean structure on $\widetilde V$. Then the trivial flat $\widetilde\mathcal{F}$-partial connection $\widetilde\nabla$ on $\widetilde V$ is a Hermitean connection, and projects to a flat $\mathcal{F}$-partial Hermitean connection $\nabla$ on $V$. Via the canonical identity $\mathbb{C} \equiv \mathbb{R}^2$, $\widetilde V$ and $V$ become oriented real vector bundles of rank 2, with trivial Riemannian structures so that $\widetilde\nabla$ and $\nabla$ are flat $\mathcal{F}$-partial Riemannian connections.  Then $\Omega^0(\mathcal{F}, V) = C^\infty(M; V)$ (the space of smooth sections of $V$), which can be considered as the subspace of $C^\infty(\widetilde M; \widetilde V) \equiv C^\infty(\widetilde M, \mathbb{C})$ consisting of the smooth functions $f: \widetilde M \to \mathbb{C}$ satisfying the equivariance condition
\begin{equation}\label{equivariant}
f(x+2\pi m, y+2\pi n) = e^{2\pi n \sin(x) i} f(x, y)\quad(m,n\in\mathbb{Z})\;.
\end{equation}
Such a function $f$ satisfies $d_{\widetilde\mathcal{F}}(f)=0$ if and only if it depends only on $x$; say $f = f(x)$. Then \Cref{equivariant} means that
\[
f(x) = e^{2\pi n \sin(x) i} f(x)\quad(n\in\mathbb{Z})\;,
\]
If $\sin(x)$ is irrational, then the set $\{\,e^{2\pi m \sin(x) i}\mid m\in\mathbb{Z}\,\}$ is dense in the complex unit circle $\{\,z\in\mathbb{C}\mid|z|=1\,\}$. So the corresponding section $s \in C^\infty(M; V)$ is invariant by multiplication by complex numbers of modulus 1 on the leaves $\{[x]\} \times \mathbb{S}^1$ with $\sin(x)$ irrational. So $s$ vanishes on those leaves, whose union is dense in $M$, and therefore $s$ vanishes on $M$. This shows that $\ker d_\mathcal{F} = 0$ in $\Omega^0(\mathcal{F}, V)$.

On the other hand, the function $f(x,y) = e^{y \sin(x) i}$ satisfies \Cref{equivariant} and is equal to 1 on $2\pi \mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{R}$. So it defines a section $s\in C^\infty(M;V)$ satisfying $\Delta_\mathcal{F} s = 0$ on the leaf $L_0 =  \{ [0] \} \times \mathbb{S}^1$. Then $s_t := e^{-t\Delta_\mathcal{F}}s$ remains independent of $t>0$ on $L_0$, and therefore the restriction to $2\pi \mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{R}$ of its lift to $\widetilde M$ remains equal to $f$ for all $t$. If the limit of $s_t$ as $t \to \infty$ were defined in $C^\infty(M;V)$, it would be in $\ker d_\mathcal{F}$ and different from zero on $L_0$, a contradiction.

In this case, the principal $O(2)$-bundle $F$ of orthonormal frames of $V$ over $M$ is the quotient of the bundle $\widetilde F := \widetilde M\times \{\,z\in\mathbb{C}\mid|z|=1\,\}$ over $\widetilde M$ by the action of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ defined by the transformations $T_{m,n}$ ($m,n \in\mathbb{Z}$). The foliation $\widehat\mathcal{F}$ on $F$ is the quotient of the foliation $\widetilde\mathcal{F}$ on $\widetilde F$ whose leaves are the fibers of the first factor projection to $\mathbb{R}$. $\widehat\mathcal{F}$ is not Riemannian because its leaf closures do not define a stratified structure of $F$ (see Section~5.4 of \cite{Molino1988}).
